workspace_owners.summary: Lifecycle owner of the single recursive watchdog watch; classifies and bounds workspace change events into awareness and the dirty-path queue; shares one observer across in-process leases and coordinates cross-process ownership.
Per-workspace awareness state that records dirty paths, watch-active/live-fallback mode, and freshness; shared across equivalent in-process consumers so duplicate leases do not multiply observation.
Advisory cross-process coordination so concurrent workflows against the same workspace share one watch owner without weakening isolation; released exactly when the final in-process lease tears down.
Bounded workspace read/write boundary: snapshots, idempotent writes, mkdirs, copy, and listing that respect roots, excludes, inaccessible content, links, cycles, and size caps.

Five-category storage inventory and cleanup planner; reports eligibility reason, bytes/counts, recreatability, owner, and recovery impact; protects active run IDs, explicit retention, and the last recoverable state.

Run-start retention and recovery sweeper: registers active run IDs and temporary-path owners, reclaims stale temporary/operational/derived data, and preserves required artifacts, evidence, and recoverable state.
Single ReindexWriter pipeline that hashes a deterministic manifest, reuses unchanged rows, publishes generations atomically, and processes only affected files on localized change.
Persisted dirty-path queue that unifies observer events and MCP mutations; coalesces bursts by final path state and drains pending marks into the single reindex writer.
Lifecycle hooks that hand dirty paths to the persisted explore queue and ReindexWriter; removes recurring refreshes that do work solely because a phase or loop repeats.
Agent-facing search/navigation surface: ranked files/content, symbols, structure, graph relationships, impact, and tests backed by source evidence with freshness and fallback metadata.
Atomic history archival and bounded pruning for workflow records; protects the last valid recoverable state across interrupted or failed publication.
Pipeline entry that registers the active run ID, runs retention on start, reconciles interrupted work on restart, and unregisters the active run on every terminal path.
Canonical atomic-write primitive: repeating an operation with unchanged retained content creates no persistent content change, duplicate history, or unnecessary refresh.
Shared filesystem backend interface that consolidates bounded read/write/stat/exists/list operations behind the canonical boundary used by workspace and artifact code.
Concrete Path-backed implementation of FileBackend; the lowest-level atomic-replace/fsync/unlink boundary that every consolidated write routes through.
Canonical template reader/cache boundary that consolidates filesystem reads of packaged and project prompt templates behind a shared registry.
Master-prompt materialization boundary that writes the durable prompt snapshot through the canonical idempotent primitive rather than raw filesystem calls.
Typed process executor that owns bounded subprocess execution, termination grace, and output decoding; the sole product-owned boundary for invoking external processes.
Process lifecycle manager that owns typed process construction and bounded termination; the canonical allowlist site for raw os-fd and child-spawn calls.

Default typed process factory boundary re-exported by the process manager package; the canonical entry point that selects the ProcessManager's sync/async/pty backend without exposing raw subprocess construction.
Logging configurator that adds buffered file sinks (buffering=8192) so high-volume operational records finalize without per-event durable rewrites.

watch_consumers.scope: Recursive workspace root (single watch per canonical workspace identity).
watch_consumers.purpose: Detect meaningful workspace changes made by agents, users, and external tools and forward bounded dirty paths into awareness and the explore dirty queue.
watch_consumers.start_owner: WorkspaceMonitor.start() schedules exactly one recursive observer, attaching to an existing in-process shared watch when present.
watch_consumers.stop_owner: WorkspaceMonitor.stop() releases the observer, cross-process lock, scheduler, and awareness state on success, cancellation, failure, restart, and abnormal-exit recovery.
watch_consumers.sharing: Equivalent in-process consumers share one observer through a weak-lease table; concurrent processes coordinate through CrossProcessWatchLock without weakening isolation.
watch_consumers.exclusions: Ralph-managed paths (logs, records, temporary data, derived index state) are classified and excluded before they become activity or dirty work.
watch_consumers.capacity_failure_behavior: Predicted or actual watch exhaustion enters a bounded live-fallback mode that reports cause, freshness impact, automatic recovery, and safest next action; it never silently serves stale knowledge as current.

watch_consumers.scope: Per-workspace advisory lock coordinating equivalent observers across processes.
watch_consumers.purpose: Prevent concurrent processes from registering duplicate recursive watches on the same workspace.
watch_consumers.start_owner: WorkspaceMonitor._acquire_cross_process_watch_lock() claims the lock before scheduling a new observer.
watch_consumers.stop_owner: WorkspaceMonitor.stop() releases the lock only when the final in-process lease tears down the shared observer, using the owner id stored on the shared watch.
watch_consumers.sharing: Inter-process: the first process to claim the lock owns the observer; later processes enter live fallback and reconcile through bounded live reads.
watch_consumers.exclusions: No watch is scheduled while another process holds the lock; the lock is advisory and does not weaken process isolation.
watch_consumers.capacity_failure_behavior: When the lock cannot be acquired, awareness is set to live_fallback with the cross_process_holder cause and automatic recovery on the next lease.

watch_consumers.scope: Per-workspace awareness state shared across equivalent in-process leases.
watch_consumers.purpose: Record dirty paths and observation mode so duplicate consumers read one awareness record instead of registering duplicate observation.
watch_consumers.start_owner: awareness_for_workspace() returns the shared instance; WorkspaceMonitor sets it watch-active on a successful start.
watch_consumers.stop_owner: release_workspace_awareness() is called when the final lease tears down the shared observer.
watch_consumers.sharing: In-process: a ClassVar table keyed by canonical workspace identity; weak references allow garbage collection once no lease remains.
watch_consumers.exclusions: Internal Ralph activity is filtered by the change classifier before reaching awareness.
watch_consumers.capacity_failure_behavior: set_live_fallback() marks awareness with the bounded cause so consumers reconcile through bounded live workspace behavior.

storage_classes.growth_trigger: New durable plans, results, evidence, and recovery records produced by workflow phases.
storage_classes.user_value: Authoritative workflow output and recovery state required for correctness and audit.
storage_classes.retention_bound: Bounded by artifact history pruning and run-start retention sweeps.
storage_classes.cleanup_result: Identical-content rewrites create no persistent change; superseded history is pruned to a bounded count.
storage_classes.recreatability: Not recreatable; durable workflow records are protected from cleanup and deletion.
storage_classes.recovery_impact: Interrupted publication preserves the last valid result; cleanup never removes required artifacts or evidence.

storage_classes.growth_trigger: Artifact and receipt writes routed through the shared backend.
storage_classes.user_value: Single consolidation boundary for all workflow-record persistence.
storage_classes.retention_bound: Bounded by the idempotent-write and history layers above it.
storage_classes.cleanup_result: No independent cleanup; delegates durability to the canonical atomic-write primitive.
storage_classes.recreatability: Not recreatable; persists required workflow records.
storage_classes.recovery_impact: Atomic replace protects the last valid state across partial writes.

storage_classes.user_value: Lowest-level atomic-replace/fsync boundary that every consolidated write routes through.
storage_classes.retention_bound: Bounded by the callers above; this module is the abstraction, not a growth source.
storage_classes.cleanup_result: No independent cleanup; provides the atomic primitives callers use.
storage_classes.recreatability: Not recreatable; persists required workflow records.
storage_classes.recovery_impact: Atomic rename + fsync preserves recoverability across crashes.

storage_classes.growth_trigger: Source changes that produce new/updated symbols, chunks, structure, and graph rows.
storage_classes.user_value: Fast evidence-backed codebase search, navigation, relationships, impact, and tests.
storage_classes.retention_bound: Derived and disposable; rebuilt incrementally from project content on change.
storage_classes.cleanup_result: Deleting derived intelligence is isolated and safely rebuildable; a no-change refresh reprocesses nothing.
storage_classes.recreatability: Fully recreatable from project content via a bounded full refresh.
storage_classes.recovery_impact: When unavailable, rebuilding, or degraded, a correct live-workspace path preserves useful agent work without misrepresenting results.

storage_classes.growth_trigger: Indexed symbols, chunks, structure, and graph edges derived from project content.
storage_classes.user_value: Backing store for ranked search, structure, graph, impact, and test discovery.
storage_classes.retention_bound: Disposable derived data; bounded by the source content it indexes.
storage_classes.cleanup_result: Removal does not affect project content or workflow records; rebuild produces equivalent logical results.
storage_classes.recreatability: Fully recreatable; rebuild equivalence is verified.
storage_classes.recovery_impact: Absence triggers bounded live-search fallback, never stale results presented as current.

storage_classes.growth_trigger: Each artifact overwrite archives the prior version for audit and recovery.
storage_classes.user_value: Durable history of plans, results, and evidence supporting recovery and review.
storage_classes.retention_bound: Bounded by prune_artifact_history to a configurable count per artifact.
storage_classes.cleanup_result: prune_artifact_history reclaims superseded archives while protecting the last valid recoverable state.
storage_classes.recreatability: Not recreatable; archives are durable records of prior workflow output.
storage_classes.recovery_impact: Protects the last valid recoverable state across interrupted or failed publication.

storage_classes.growth_trigger: Diagnostic log events emitted during active workflow execution.
storage_classes.user_value: Diagnostics for debugging, attribution, and health reporting.
storage_classes.retention_bound: Bounded by buffered sinks (buffering=8192) and log rotation; finalized at completion without per-event durable rewrites.
storage_classes.cleanup_result: Stale operational logs are reclaimed by retention sweeps; active workflows are protected.
storage_classes.recreatability: Replaceable; operational logs are not required workflow records.
storage_classes.recovery_impact: Loss does not affect project content or required workflow records.

storage_classes.growth_trigger: Replaceable or incomplete data used during active work; stale completion sentinels, receipt dirs, session and scratch files.
storage_classes.user_value: Bounded temporary workspace for in-flight workflows; reclamation prevents unbounded growth.
storage_classes.retention_bound: Reclaimed during recovery and normal cleanup once no active run owns the data.
storage_classes.cleanup_result: Safely removes incomplete data while preserving active-run ownership and the last recoverable state.
storage_classes.recreatability: Replaceable; temporary data is regenerated by the workflow that needs it.
storage_classes.recovery_impact: Failed, cancelled, and interrupted work leaves no permanent temporary growth; recovery reclaims safely removable data.

storage_classes.growth_trigger: Cleanup preview and planning across all five categories.
storage_classes.user_value: Operator-visible eligibility, bytes/counts, recreatability, owner, and recovery impact before any deletion.
storage_classes.retention_bound: Planning surface; the categories it previews each have their own bound.
storage_classes.cleanup_result: Preview reports what cleanup reclaims and protects; concurrent cleanup is ownership-safe.
storage_classes.recreatability: The planner is stateless; preview reflects current storage state.
storage_classes.recovery_impact: Cleanup protects active workflows, required records, explicitly retained data, and the last recoverable state.
